newsitem.title: UK: Novo Nordisk enzyme cures washday pinks.
newsitem.headline: Novo Nordisk enzyme cures washday pinks.

text.p: A new enzyme product that bleaches the water instead of the clothes in a washer could make pink underwear a thing of the past, New Scientist magazine reported on Thursday.
The enzyme, based on an extract from the inkcap fungus, bleaches dye out only after it has washed out of the clothing, it said.
"Our system will bleach virtually any dye," Anders Pedersen, a researcher at Danish biotechnology company Novo Nordisk told New Scientist.
The enzyme works together with hydrogen peroxide and the organic compound phenothiazine-10-propionic acid, they said.
It could be introduced in low enough amounts to where it did not put clothes at risk, Pedersen said -- but it would not totally do away with the need to sort a wash.
"We would never go so far as to say you could throw everything in together," he said.
"But it would help in cases where people haven't sorted garments properly, so a single red sock ends up in the wash."
The company said it was talking to washing powder manufacturers.
